contacts.offered: A finding (21 of their agents point at unreadable documents) and a paid Sentinel check inside a leash.
contacts.result: Leash confirmed the finding and fixed the two documents, which resolve since 7 October. The early passkey-owned registrations cannot be re-pointed, since the account exposes no setAgentURI. They took the seller-side fit on one condition: a LeashAccount pays by direct transfer only, no EIP-3009 and no ERC-1271, so it emits Paid(agent, seller, token, amount, ref, remainingToday) instead of signing an authorization. Sentinel now accepts that receipt on mainnet, with nine checks including pinning the Paid log to accountOf(agent) read off the Leash hub, so a contract that merely emits a matching event is refused. We accept USDC only: the network's test dollar has an unpermissioned mint capped at 100.000000 tUSD per call, which leashGate accepts by default. They offered to make a real paid call from a leashed agent on mainnet once we accepted pay(), which is now true. On 2026-10-10 Leash made the paid call: a Claude Desktop agent on a $1 a day leash that allows only our payee called Sentinel through leash-monad-mcp, paid 0.01 USDC from inside the leash and got its verdict. The Paid event shows $0.99 left on the leash. Leash added the transaction to its README and to `npx leash-monad verify`. They also fixed the tUSD finding in leash-monad 0.1.6, credited it in SECURITY.md and accepted our PR for an opt-in sellerPolicy that pays only sellers with a live Sclera bond.

contacts.offered: A recomputer for Aqueous records (an agent was never paid before delivering), sent as a PR, with the first rule committed and funded by us.
contacts.result: Dissent merged our recomputer for the Aqueous escrow (PR #7, merge 0f15d30) after two review rounds. Their CI passed. Their review found a real flaw (any token accepted), which we fixed by pinning Circle USDC. Recomputer 0x4d1A62869D16AB2Bac95408445129C4927f88457, Sourcify verified. We posted a fork rehearsal of all nine steps; Alnitak replayed it independently and found a launcher flaw that could hide a failed step, which we fixed in follow-up PR #8. Both are merged. The reviewed policy is now registered and active on Monad mainnet, policy id 0x52655800591f954bb48cfd67e41475ec394898cd8e2e1cd8a7fa3350f7c479f8. We read that registration off chain: deposit 0.1 MON, recompute 1,500,000, validate 200,000, maxEvidenceLen 32, which matches the reviewed parameters exactly. On 2026-10-10 the first coordinated case ran live on Monad mainnet, two parties each signing their own steps. Our agent committed a 0.75 MON bounty that no Aqueous job of ours is paid out before delivery (commitment 0x39cc82c881281f204b397f10ac173df54afc9d77e5f6385195c717e32e4aed8a). Our buyer then released a 0.10 USDC job early with no delivery recorded. Alnitak's challenger sealed, revealed and withdrew: ChallengeSucceeded, value 1 against threshold 0, 0.85 MON paid out (the bounty plus his 0.1 MON deposit back). He confirmed every receipt in the thread. Framing agreed by both sides: a coordinated early-release demonstration by one operator, not a discovered exploit and not agent misconduct. Dissent then published the case on its own site, crediting Kanmani's recomputer with links to the receipts.

contacts.offered: A finding: their ERC-8004 outcome feedback commits a hash whose document is served nowhere, so nobody can verify it. Two fixes plus a sponsored Sclera bond on agents 10280 and 10315.
contacts.result: They replied on 2026-10-15 and merged a fix (PR 2) so the feedbackURI route serves JSON. On 2026-10-22 production still returns 404 OUTCOME_NOT_FOUND for agent 10315's two feedbacks. Their code rebuilds the document from an in-memory table that starts empty on a cold start. We rebuilt both documents from their own repo, checked each hash against the posting transaction's calldata. We then opened PR 8 to serve them. Not merged, nothing verified yet. Agent 10280's document could not be rebuilt.
